content_html_sanitized:
Posted February 14, 2003

I try to keep MarijuanaNews on-topic focused on cannabis for two major reasons.

First and foremost, the cannabis issues are quite complex enough, thank you. I really don't need anything else to write about.

Second, whatever one's views on other subjects may be, cannabis prohibition still makes no sense. There are Conservative anti-prohibitionists, Liberal, anti-prohibitionists, and Socialist anti-prohibitionists. I have friends in all of these categories.

This certainly applies to the debate over the pending Iraqi war, but there are times when the cannabis issues impinge on other issues, and this is one of those times.

I remember a cartoon that I saw many years ago with two kids at the breakfast table looking skeptically at their cereal. The boy says to his mother, You lied to us about pot, so how do we know that you aren't lying to us about granola?

Of course, there is one real-world example of this credibility problem that directly relates to lying about cannabis.

Recently, Mitch Earleywine, the author of " Understanding Marijuana " (Oxford University Press, 2002) wrote, one gateway effect probably is real: When kids try cannabis, they realize that the propaganda they've been fed is untrue. They don't take an axe to their siblings or flunk out of high school. They don't get terrorists showing up at their doors for cash. And they start to suspect that what they've been told about other drugs is equally false.

That's not just a theory. I teach a university class about the science of drugs, and every year my students describe similar experiences.

Cannabis does not cause kids to try harder drugs, but lying to them about it does.
See
Marijuana, Gateways, and Circuses
and
The Gateway Theory Won't Die Because It Tells Prohibitionists Something They Want to Believe, But The Truth Tells Them Something They Refuse to Hear.
and links

However, the problem of credibility goes far beyond drugs and granola, and lying about cannabis has been extended to the War on Terror as well.
See
The Endless Cynicism of the Drug Warriors. The Drug War and Terrorism. MarijuanaNews Analysis by Richard Cowan
and
Afghan Opium Crop Booms Under DEAland Control As Feds Focus On Cannabis, Reverse Policy On Prosecuting Small Medical Growers In Washington State; Cut 6 Plants In California; Seize Bongs In Illinois.

Thus, it is not the opponents of cannabis prohibition who are stretching the point, reaching for a connection, but the leaders of the Drug War, the leaders of the Free World.

However, the question of credibility is key to everything, every aspect of life, but especially the justification for the use of force. That is why there is a Commandment against giving false witness lying to justify community violence, particularly against members of one's own community.
See
Mormon Church Newspaper Violates The Ninth Commandment. Gives False Evidence Against Marijuana Users and Anti-Prohibitionists.

The question of credibility is absolutely vital at a time when governments in democratic societies are saying that they need more police power to go after terrorists. We are told that we must be prepared to give up some of our freedom, some of our privacy, so that our governments can protect us from those who demonstrably mean us harm.

But it does not follow that just because the danger is real, the competence and trustworthiness of our self-proclaimed protectors are therefore also real. In fact, there is every reason to distrust them and doubt their competence. They utterly failed to protect us on September 11th, 2001, in part because they were less interested in stopping foreign terrorists than in stopping drugs.
See
Did The Drug War Claim Another 3,056 Casualties On 9-11? Ariana Huffington's Extraordinary Indictment.

They seem to have learned nothing since then. Even as New York City was under a terrorist watch, the New York City police did not stop seeking out marijuana users. That should have been the real story instead of puns, when the Dell Dude was held over night in jail.
See
Dude, You're Getting A Journalism Lesson. The Media Won't Report How Many Cannabis Arrests There Are In DEAland, or New York City, But This Celebrity Arrest Is Even Reported In The Washington Post.

Are the people of New York really supposed to feel safer with their police thus preoccupied? That is incompetence on a scale that defies easy measurement.

Can anyone seriously argue that the massive police resources devoted to arresting cannabis users and eradicating the hemp plant would not be better used hunting bombers?

And, as for trusting their honesty and honorable intentions, how is that possible when the Drug Czar lies to justify arresting hundreds of thousands of Americans.
See
Walters Tells a New Lie. Oh Happy Day! People Need Treatment If They Are Sent to Treatment, By Definition. And How Do They Treat Marijuana Addicts? We Couldn't Make This Up, But They Did.

And the Bush Administration, which promised to uphold states rights, denies jurors the right to hear about state laws.
See
Jury Tampering Federal Judge Extorts Guilty Verdict From Terrified Citizens In Major States Rights Case. Rosenthal Conviction Versus the Constitution.

They also sought to deprive doctors of the right even to discuss the medical use of cannabis with their patients.
See
Bush Administration Argues That Freedom of Speech Applies to Pharmaceutical Company Ads , But Not Conversations Between Doctors and Patients About Medical Cannabis. We Couldn't Make This Up!

These are not the actions of friends of freedom. Those to whom the American people have entrusted their freedom are more than willing to abuse their power.
See
The Narking of America: The Bush Team for Total War, or Just to Keep the Lid On.

Today, the government of DEAland is engaged in a massive prohibitionist propaganda campaign focused largely on marijuana that is almost as ubiquitous as portraits of Saddam Hussein in Baghdad.

No, I am not comparing George W. Bush with the Iraqi dictator.

We are told, so it must be true, that Saddam actually enjoys seeing his victims suffer. I am sure George Bush would not. No, he would never visit a hospice and smile his little smile while listening to the screams of agony of those who are deprived of adequate pain relief.

He is certainly too kind a person to visit cancer wards and laugh as people wretch their guts out because the pharmaceutical anti-emetics do not work for them, or they simply cannot afford them, and they cannot get access to cannabis.
See
 " Bill chose not to inhale, I'd like the same choice. " -- A Teenage Cancer Patient.

I am quite certain that he would not enjoy seeing DEA agents handcuff a paralysed woman in her bed while they cut down her plants to protect her from her dealer.
See
The Prohibitionist Police State Versus The People. Analysis By Richard Cowan

No, he would never do that, so he is morally far superior to the sadistic Saddam, but is he more believable?

We are called upon to commit the ultimate act of trust and follow our leaders to war, so we must ask that our leaders prove themselves to be believable. That they have not done.

It may well be that we should liberate Iraq, but shouldn't we first liberate ourselves?

And to those who protest for peace with Iraq, should you not first be protesting for peace at home?
